units.title: 1. Types of Inherited Neuropathy and CMT-1 vs CMT-2
units.guide:
Demyelinating inherited neuropathies are CMTD and Refsum's; axonal are FAP (transthyretin: wild type senile systemic amyloidosis, mutant FAP), porphyria and Tangier's.
Acute neuropathies are predominantly demyelinating (AIDP, GBS) with acute intermittent porphyria the axonal exception.
CMT combines motor and sensory involvement (HMSN); HSAN is its autonomic variant. CMT-1 and CMT-2 are both autosomal dominant; CMT-1 is more common, demyelinating with onion bulbs, nerve thickening and early onset, CMT-2 axonal, mild and later.

units.title: 2. CMT-4, Features of CMT-1 and Thickened Nerves
units.guide:
CMT-4 (Dejerine sottas) is AD/AR congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy. CMT-1 has a long slow 10-30 year course with pes cavus as the m/c presentation, hammer toes, palpable hypertrophic nerves, positive family history and mild kyphosis in 1/10th.
Sensory symptoms are absent although large-fibre signs are positive; motor disease is distal > proximal, lower limb predominant, non-debilitating with slow conduction, normal amplitude, prolonged distal latency and temporal dispersion, ending in inverted champagne leg.
Reflexes show generalised hypo/areflexia with ankle jerk universally absent; thickened nerves occur in leprosy, CIDP and CMT.

units.title: 3. Familial Amyloid Polyneuropathy and Porphyric Neuropathy
units.guide:
FAP is mutant transthyretin axonal sensory-motor polyneuropathy with ANS involvement, painful neuropathy and large + small fibre symptoms.
Porphyric neuropathy manifests as neurovisceral (AIP) or less common cutaneous (variegate, hereditary coproporphyria with blisters, hyperpigmentation, hypertrichosis, skin fragility).
It is autosomal dominant with predominant ANS plus PNS and CNS involvement, acute onset, females > males, 3rd-4th decade and menstruation as precipitant; GIT acute abdominal pain is the most frequent symptom and neuropathy is acute axonal, proximal predominant with rare sensory glove-and-stocking or bathing suite pattern.

units.title: 4. Porphyric ANS and CNS Features, Tangier's and Refsum Disease
units.guide:
ANS features are the hallmark of porphyric neuropathy: orthostatic hypotension, erectile dysfunction, urinary incontinence, persistent tachycardia > bradycardia and labile hypertension leading to hypertensive encephalopathy (PRES).
CNS features include mild neuropsychiatric symptoms, seizures, motor > sensory neuropathy, facial and bulbar weakness progressing to GBS-like flaccid quadriparesis with respiratory involvement, and rapidly progressive wasting from anterior horn cell involvement; SIADH causes hyponatremia.
Tangier's is autosomal recessive with an ATP binding cascade protein defect, low HDL, orange tonsil, axonal asymmetric mononeuropathy. Refsum's is demyelinating from a phytanic oxidase (alpha-oxidation) defect with the triad retinitis pigmentosa, cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy.

units.title: 5. Romberg's Sign, Wash Basin Sign, Fabry's and Autonomic Neuropathies
units.guide:
Romberg's sign components are semicircular canal, vestibulo-cerebellar fibres, visual stimulus and proprioception; standing with mild flexed posture and hands close to body eliminates the first two and eye closure eliminates vision, isolating proprioception.
The wash basin sign shows improper posture plus no visual component with posterior column tract disorder giving no compensation and a fall.
Fabry's disease shows angiokeratoma with painful acroparesthesia (painful small fibre neuropathy), digital paresthesia, severe ANS symptoms, axonal pathology and renal manifestation; autonomic neuropathies are seen in diabetes, amyloidosis, porphyria, Fabry and vincristine.
